**Monsters die differently every time.** DOOM plays each monster's death
the same way from one angle; now the killing blow decides how it goes. Death
frames are retimed for every kill (a snap, a hesitation then a drop, a
slump), monsters killed by one rocket fall out of step on purpose, bodies
fall away from the blow and settle as they land, and now and then a hit off
the middle turns a monster or a hard push steps it back. Monsters on two
legs can also fall in ways their drawings never show, on joints placed by
hand for the zombieman, shotgun guy and chaingunner, or found in the art for
others: a low hit sweeps the legs, a hard one is a chest blast that throws
the body, and a killing head shot cuts the strings. Every hit also pushes,
so living monsters flinch and spring back. All of it is drawing only; the
game, its damage and demos are unchanged. F4 → Combat has a switch for each
piece, a **Reaction strength** slider, and **Dying turn to face you** (off by
default).

**Wound holes.** Bullets and pellets shoot see-through holes in monsters,
with ragged bloody edges and dark rims in the WAD's own colours. The holes
follow the animation, widen with close hits and stay on the corpse. F4 →
Wound holes.

**Free aim.** With mouse look, bullets now go exactly where you look, even
with a monster in front of you: aim at the head and you hit the head, aim
past and you miss. For DOOM's autoaim, turn on F4 → **Classic aim** (off by
default). Rockets, plasma and the BFG aim as before, and demos and netgames
keep vanilla aiming.

**Windows break into real pieces.** A shot pane now breaks into large,
irregular shards, smaller near the hit, with the same stepped pixel edges as
the glass left in the frame. They tumble, catch reflections while flying,
bounce and lie flat and matte on the floor. The sound was rebuilt to match: a
hard crack, then each piece catching the frame, falling, rebounding and
tipping over its edges, at 22 kHz so the bright clatter survives. A breaking
window is also heard twice as far.

**Heavier footsteps.** Your steps are heavy combat boots now, coloured by the
floor, harder when running and when landing from a fall. After each step
your kit settles: buckles with a light weapon, a long gun on its sling, the
rocket launcher or BFG thudding, and armour clicking when you wear it. More
floors are recognised correctly, carpet among them, and steps and room echoes
now always agree on what a floor is made of.

**Sound fades as it does in air.** Far sounds lose half their strength each
time the distance doubles, instead of DOOM's straight fade that keeps
monsters across the room almost as loud as nearby ones. Gunfire and
explosions carry farther, faint and dull. F4 → Sound → **Natural distance
falloff** (on by default; DOOM only).

**Near misses whiz.** An enemy's bullet from far off that passes close by
whistles past your head, so you know you're under fire.

**Rooms sound like what they're made of.** Rough stone and dirt scatter the
echoes and the room goes flat; smooth metal panels keep it ringing. Each echo
also loses the treble its walls take, and a texture's painted seams and
cracks make a surface sound a little rougher.

**Smaller fixes.** Screens stay on while the lamps in their flickering room
blink. A switched-off screen keeps its glass whole, and a shot-out lamp in a
glowing room stays dead instead of pulsing. Glowing liquid edges no longer
double up on walls that paint their own edge.
